steps.description: I need to create a Python script that implements the described numerical experiment to test whether neural network generalization behavior probes solution space rigidity. The script will: (1) define abstract constraints (e.g., polynomial interpolation or functional equation constraints), (2) sweep over constraint count w, (3) for each w, find minimum hidden layer width N_c(w) that achieves zero violation on held-out constraints, (4) measure the trend of N_c(w) vs w. This is a pure ML/math experiment with no physical system mapping. I will write the script to run in the workspace directory and ensure it produces reproducible numerical results.

plans.objective: [DIM: STRUCTURE] If the constraint manifold has low intrinsic dimensionality, N_c(w) will remain constant after a critical width w_c where the network capacity first exceeds the degrees of freedom in the constraint space.

steps.description: [auto-routed: surprise=1.00] Create a Python script that implements the bootstrap rigidity test for neural networks. The script will: (1) generate synthetic constraint functions with known intrinsic dimensionality (low-dim = rigid, high-dim = fat), (2) train small feedforward networks of varying widths w, (3) measure N_c(w) as the minimum width needed to achieve zero violations on held-out constraints for each constraint sample count w, (4) output the (w, N_c(w)) table and plot. This directly tests the hypothesis that low intrinsic dimensionality causes N_c(w) to plateau after w_c. The script will be self-contained and runnable without external physics tools.
